name: African feminism
summary: African feminism is a set of theories and movements, not one doctrine, that seek equality and improved status for women on the continent while grounding the project in African cultures and histories rather than Western models. Its mainstream holds that patriarchy was strengthened by colonialism and persists through neo-colonial structures, that oppressions of sex, class and race combine, and that men should be partners in change. Strands such as nego-feminism, stiwanism and Motherism differ on method (negotiation versus transformation), on family and motherhood, and especially on sexuality.
scope: The mainstream of continental African feminisms since the 1980s as set out by Molara Ogundipe-Leslie (stiwanism), Obioma Nnaemeka (nego-feminism) and the 2003 Maputo Protocol, with Motherism and Awa Thiam's multiple jeopardy as supporting strands. Diaspora-focused womanism and Africana womanism and particular national women's movements are excluded. Much of the test (economics, defence, tech) is outside what the sources address, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

sources.title: African feminism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of strands (stiwanism, nego-feminism, Motherism, womanism), views on colonialism, family, religion, sexuality, men, land and state.

sources.author: Obioma Nnaemeka, Signs 29(2), 2004
sources.usedFor: A defining statement of nego-feminism: critique of Western feminist theory and development discourse, negotiation, inclusion of men, women's economic practice.

sources.title: Maputo Protocol
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Contents, ratification and objections to the African Union's 2003 women's rights treaty.

sources.title: Molara Ogundipe
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Stiwanism: structural and colonial account of patriarchy, work with men, rejection of Euro-American definitions.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The Maputo Protocol commits states to women's health services, so adherents would back public provision, though the sources give no view on universal systems as such.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Concern for women's economic burdens and informal-sector poverty points to support for better pay, but the sources never discuss minimum wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Nnaemeka ties development discourse to imperial processes and stresses women's own economic strategies, suggesting scepticism of market triumphalism; not directly stated.

public-ownership.rationale: African feminist writing is concerned with class and neo-colonial structures but does not set out a position on nationalising industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Ogundipe-Leslie's stiwanism treats class as shaping women's experience, which implies support for redistribution, though taxes are not discussed.

unions-good.rationale: Women's collective organising is celebrated in the sources, so unions are likely welcomed, but labour unions specifically are not discussed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Sources stress that women were denied land and inheritance under colonial and customary rule, implying property rights are not treated as absolute; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Opposition to neo-colonial structures suggests support for regulating foreign and domestic firms, an inference not stated in the sources.

cut-welfare.rationale: The Maputo Protocol's economic and social welfare rights for women imply opposition to cutting support, though welfare policy is not debated.

worker-ownership.rationale: The sources discuss women's cooperative and savings practices but give no view on worker ownership of firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: African feminist writing has no recorded stance on surveillance and terrorism.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is outside the sources; adherents would not obviously agree on it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses hate speech law; adherents' views on it are not documented.

strong-leader.rationale: The Maputo Protocol's push for participation in decision-making implies preference for inclusive politics over strongman rule; inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: North African state feminism and the Maputo Protocol assume the state as a vehicle for women's rights, which contradicts anti-statism; inferred.

limit-guns.rationale: The Protocol's concern with violence against women in peacetime and war suggests support for limiting weapons, though guns are not addressed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Feminist concern with state and wartime violence against women leans against expanding police and military power; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sources do not discuss sex work; African feminists are divided on sexuality questions generally.

rehabilitation.rationale: The Protocol's emphasis on dignity and humane treatment implies rehabilitative justice, which the sources do not discuss directly.

decide-locally.rationale: Nnaemeka values locally defined priorities in development, yet feminists also use national and continental law for women's rights, so this is split.

traditional-family.rationale: Sources show many African feminists value family and communalism (Motherism, Aidoo) while fighting patriarchal norms within it, so they are split on this wording.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Nyanzi notes the bulk of African feminists resist challenging heterosexism while a minority of queer feminists push for it, so adherents are split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Article 14 of the Maputo Protocol permits abortion only in limited cases such as rape, incest and risk to health, which falls short of legal in most cases.

more-religion-public.rationale: Islamic and Christian-influenced feminisms exist alongside secular ones, and the sources show no consensus on religion's public role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: African feminists tie women's status to colonial and racial hierarchies and reject Western white-feminist framing, which supports active correction of historical injustice.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources describe African feminisms as aiming to change culture as it affects women, treating gender roles as made by societies and colonialism, though some stress complementarity.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: African feminists defend African cultural practice against Western imposition (Nnaemeka) but also aim to modify culture where it harms women (Nkealah).

gradual-change.rationale: Nego-feminism and snail-sense feminism favour negotiated, strategic progress while stiwanism calls for comprehensive transformation, so the school is split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The sources do not address immigration; solidarity with African and diaspora women points against restriction.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Feminists use AU and UN instruments such as the Maputo Protocol, yet distrust Western-led international agendas (Nnaemeka), so views are mixed.

free-trade.rationale: Nnaemeka links development discourse to imperial processes, suggesting suspicion of unregulated global trade; not directly stated.

nation-first.rationale: No documented position; anti-imperial leanings are balanced by use of international women's rights law.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Nnaemeka criticises Western feminists who claim a moral duty to rescue African women, implying scepticism of interventions in their name.

open-borders.rationale: Migration is not discussed in the sources.

limit-growth.rationale: The sources stress women's need for livelihoods and development, which makes limiting growth unlikely to appeal; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Women's central role in food production (over 70 percent in East Africa) implies concern for climate threats, though climate is not directly discussed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Sources are silent on technology; no documented view.

expand-nuclear.rationale: No documented view on nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: Stiwanism calls for sweeping social transformation but the sources favour negotiation and strategy, so revolution is not stated as a method.

experts-over-public.rationale: Nnaemeka argues African women's knowledge is marginalised by outside experts and theory makers, implying distrust of expert rule.

central-planning.rationale: Economic systems are not addressed beyond class and neo-colonial critique.

socialized-markets.rationale: No documented position on market socialism.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Protocol protects women's inheritance rights, which is a different matter; heavy taxation of inheritance is not discussed, so a weak lean against.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade policy is not addressed beyond anti-neo-colonial themes.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' views on industrial policy are undocumented.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Concern with women's access to land and small enterprise (such as savings clubs and kiosks) fits widely spread small property; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nnaemeka describes women building businesses with seed money, so abolishing money and wages does not fit their economic practice.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No relevant position in the sources.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Protocol's demand for women's participation in political and decision-making processes presupposes open politics, which makes one-party rule contrary to the programme.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Sources note female chiefs lost power under colonial indirect rule, but give no view on monarchy as an institution.

democracy-best.rationale: Article 9 of the Maputo Protocol and campaigns like Kenya's #WeAre52 treat democratic participation as the route to women's equality, though voters choosing badly is not discussed.

direct-votes.rationale: The sources do not discuss referendums; women's participation is stressed but no mechanism is preferred.

workers-councils.rationale: No African feminist source proposes councils as the basis of power; the sources discuss women's organising, not this model.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Protocol's non-discrimination and equal participation principles deny that any group is naturally fit to rule, including men over women.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Protocol deals with women in armed conflict and peace, but the sources do not say whether adherents rule out all political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Feminist concern with women as victims of armed conflict and the Protocol's peace provisions make glorifying war foreign to the position.

separate-church-state.rationale: Islamic feminism works within religious frameworks while other strands are secular, so adherents are split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Feminists who work inside Islam seek gender equality within religion, but Protocol-style rights law is rooted in human rights rather than scripture; inferred lean against.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Women's access to justice is framed as a state duty under the Protocol, which does not fit privatised courts; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Feminist peace and anti-militarist emphases lean against arms competition; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Sources stress Africa's ethnic diversity and rule out a single African feminism, which sits poorly with ethnic nation-building; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class is one axis of oppression in stiwanism alongside gender and race, not described as the main driver of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Equality is the goal, but the sources do not specify equal outcomes versus opportunity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not directly addressed; women's land access is the focus.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources hold colonialism responsible for weakening women's status, which suggests sympathy for reparations, but reparations are not explicitly mentioned.

civilizational-union.rationale: The sources treat Africa as diverse and do not discuss unions based on shared civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Communalism and Motherism's nurture ethic stress community over individual self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Feminists rely on rights instruments like the Maputo Protocol, so ranking communal duties above individual rights would undercut their programme, although communal values matter to them.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Motherism places nature and nurture at the core, which suggests regard for nature's value; not stated as intrinsic.

limit-population.rationale: Article 14 stresses women's own control over reproduction, not state-imposed limits, so state population limitation is unlikely to be endorsed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The sources never judge industrial civilization as a whole; their concern is colonial structures and women's livelihoods.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Nothing in the sources on speeding up technological disruption; no documented position.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is not discussed in the sources, which centre on women's bodies in cultural context.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Automated governance is outside the sources, so no position can be documented.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy and encryption do not appear in the sources.

restore-past-order.rationale: Sources say pre-colonial gender roles were often complementary, but feminists want to modify culture rather than restore the past; Motherism is the nearest case.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Nego-feminism is pragmatic and negotiating, yet the sources do not state this as a general maxim.

direct-action.rationale: Feminists use campaigns and negotiation (#WeAre52, nego-feminism) as well as protest; the sources do not rank direct action against elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nnaemeka's no-ego, collaborative method suggests it, but it is not stated as a principle on means and ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nothing suggests a return to foraging; adherents focus on development and women's livelihoods.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Sources note gender roles as complementary pre-colonially while seeking change in unequal burdens; no stated abolition.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The sources do not set out a principle of distribution by need versus work.

production-for-use.rationale: The sources do not address profit versus production for use.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Class is part of stiwanism's analysis but the sources do not state a profit-exploitation theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The programme's commitment to participation and rights does not fit dictatorial rule; inferred.

collective-farming.rationale: The sources emphasise women's own land access and food production, not collectivisation; inferred.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The sources critique neo-colonial structures but do not claim that capitalism inevitably produces great-power war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Social and economic welfare rights for women assume state revenue, so adherents reject this; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; feminists aim to change harmful cultural practices, which sits with but is not equal to the harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nnaemeka and Akob contrast Western individualism with communal values, so rights are not held to belong only to individuals, though the Protocol uses individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Peace and anti-war emphases suggest opposition, though conscription is not discussed.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Participation in politics is central to the programme, so exit is not preferred over voice; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers conflicts with rights-based participation; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: The Protocol's economic and social welfare rights reflect the view that rights need material means to be usable.

media-academia-power.rationale: Nnaemeka criticises Western academic theory-making power over African women but does not claim universities and media outrank elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: African feminism opposes colonial and racial hierarchies and the sources give no support for racial genetic hierarchies.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and trade bodies is not discussed; the sources favour women's direct political participation.

total-state.rationale: A rights-based participatory programme cannot endorse a state directing all of life; inferred.

national-rebirth.rationale: The sources do not frame any nation as decadent or in need of rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Peace commitments and anti-imperial critique make territorial expansion alien to the position; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by personal oath contradicts equal rights and participation in the Protocol; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Opposition to exploitative colonial labour control of women makes bound labour alien to the position; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nnaemeka argues that theory formation is imperial and that African women are shut out as knowledge producers, which supports the claim that knowledge reflects power.

universal-morality.rationale: Feminists rely on universal human rights in the Maputo Protocol while resisting Western universalism, as Nnaemeka does in her critique of Okin and Nussbaum.

single-common-good.rationale: Stress on difference among African women and on negotiation among interests leans against one rationally worked-out common good; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Israel and Zionism are outside the African feminist sources used here.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed beyond Africana womanism including diaspora women.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival policy does not appear in the sources.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Participatory inclusion of women in decision-making suggests sympathy, though workplaces are not discussed.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance mechanisms are not discussed, only women's access to education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Social and economic rights suggest willingness to spend; inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: The link between political and economic freedom is not discussed in the sources.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rulers' moral example versus law is not discussed; the sources rely on legal instruments like the Protocol.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial framing and the rejection of Western definitions of African feminism suggest support for self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Peace commitments suggest opposition to unilateral force; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Motherism, religion-inclusive feminisms and cultural grounding mean reason is not held the only guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Women's rights under the Protocol are framed as universal; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Unpaid care burdens on women make work conditions harsh for women; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nego-feminism favours collaboration and compromise, but class cooperation specifically is not discussed.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: African feminists defend African heritage against erasure, so sacrificing institutions is rejected; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Nnaemeka and Ogundipe-Leslie resist Western dominance in defining African women's issues, which fits a common front, though the idea is not stated.

workers-nation.rationale: National versus international organising of workers is not addressed.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Protocol requires equality before the law, so law enforcing distinct roles is rejected, even though Motherism values complementarity socially.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest on loans is not discussed; Nnaemeka describes women's mutual savings but not a ban on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: African feminism opposes colonial racial and gender hierarchies, and the sources give no support for racial segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Stiwanism critiques colonial and neo-colonial structures but does not state a class theory of the state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production policy is not addressed in the sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigrant assimilation is not discussed in the sources.

elite-replacement.rationale: Nothing in the sources suggests a replacement conspiracy; it conflicts with the opposition to racial hierarchy.

proportional-representation.rationale: Efforts to raise women's representation in parliaments point to openness to PR, though electoral systems are not discussed.

national-mission.rationale: Anti-imperial emphasis suggests rejecting a mission to spread a government form; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Wikipedia reports that stiwanism and Thiam's multiple jeopardy locate women's oppression in structures, and Ogundipe-Leslie criticised patriarchal systems and internalised patriarchy.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Women's control over reproduction in Article 14 is incompatible with state eugenics; inferred.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Opposition to racial hierarchy and the rejection of colonial categories leave no basis for discouraging mixed marriage.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Protocol assigns the state many duties for women's welfare, education and health, which contradicts a night-watchman state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Maputo Protocol is built on non-discrimination, dignity and equal rights for women, which states equal worth and equal protection before the law.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources treat colonial domination as the source of women's lost status, which fits this view of settler states; not stated directly.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Protocol seeks equal marital and inheritance rights regardless of custom, but Muslim and customary-law objections show adherents divide on overriding personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports restricting religious choice; inferred from rights framing.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter law is not an African feminist concern in the sources.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not addressed; religion-friendly and secular strands both exist.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The doctrine of a socialist state in a hostile world is outside the sources.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Women's right to take part in political and decision-making processes in Article 9 rests on the idea that authority needs the participation of the governed.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist trade goals are not discussed; the sources note only women's historical role in trade.

population-transfer.rationale: Forcing out a minority conflicts with the Protocol's dignity and non-discrimination provisions and with peace commitments.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Nego-feminism's no-ego collaboration stresses cooperation over struggle as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are not discussed; the sources stress participation, not restrictions on parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Stiwanism treats patriarchal structures and internalised patriarchy as constraints on women whether or not used in a given case, which fits a non-domination view.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed beyond participation in government.

vanguard-party.rationale: Nnaemeka's stress on negotiation, local knowledge and women's own agency leans against a vanguard; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Stiwanism treats rural and poor women's conditions as the core concern of social transformation.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are outside the sources, though the Protocol covers adequate housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Women's collective action is valued; inferred lean against restrictions.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Stiwanism explains women's poverty by colonial and neo-colonial structures, not by population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The sources hold that Africa's diversity is a given and rule out a single feminism, without treating diversity as a threat.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of officials by lot is not discussed in the sources.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rights-based programme favours keeping protections; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls on food are not discussed, though women's food production is stressed.

party-controls-media.rationale: Participation and expression rights conflict with party control of media; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Nothing in the programme supports party command of the army; inferred from the participatory framework.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed in the sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay for elected officials is not discussed; the sources focus on women's presence in office.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is not discussed in the sources.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: African feminists use the African Union's Maputo Protocol to bind states, which implies acceptance of pooled sovereignty at continental level.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The balance of executive and legislative powers over the army is not discussed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not discussed, apart from Nana Asma'u and Islamic feminist work on women's roles.

clerical-rule.rationale: Islamic feminists work within religion but seek equality, which sits poorly with rule by senior clerics; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The sources do not discuss revolutionary defeatism in great-power wars.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: African women writers such as Emecheta are central to the tradition, which makes censorship unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Women's participation in politics favours turnover and open competition; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections are not discussed in the sources.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is outside the sources.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The Protocol protects women's right to adequate housing without abolishing renting; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Peace emphasis and violence against women concerns lean against an armed citizenry; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Ogundipe-Leslie centred rural women's hardships, not any claim that rural life is healthier.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of nations split by colonial borders is not discussed in the feminist sources used.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Nnaemeka's own critique targets Western theory, not educated people in general, and the tradition is largely academic and literary.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nnaemeka rejects the idea that Western feminism and moral universals can judge African practices, supporting a view of cultures as different rather than ranked.

death-penalty.rationale: Capital punishment is not discussed in the sources, and adherents are likely divided.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Protocol's education and reproductive-health provisions support sexual and gender education for girls and boys, though sexuality remains contested.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum disputes over evolution are not discussed in the sources.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Pornography law is not discussed in the sources; feminists elsewhere divide on it and no African consensus is documented.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not discussed in the sources.

minority-language-support.rationale: Respect for Africa's linguistic and ethnic diversity points to support, but the sources do not discuss language policy.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Protocol sets limits on harmful customary practice, while religious freedom is also valued, so adherents are split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Social nonconformity as a value is not discussed; the sources stress communal values and negotiation.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Nnaemeka's critique of imperial development discourse suggests sympathy for debt relief; not stated.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Stiwanism holds that colonial and neo-colonial structures must be transformed along with the position of women.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-writing procedure is not discussed in the sources.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rights frameworks lean against trading freedoms for growth; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nnaemeka criticises Western rescue narratives, yet solidarity and development work imply support for aid on African terms; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Peace emphasis points against nuclear arms.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Method of electing a head of state is not discussed in the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are not discussed in the sources.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Peace commitments suggest willingness to compromise on territory; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Communal values and women's land claims fit property serving broader social ends; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The character of the Soviet Union is outside the sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Care for nature and communal welfare suggest support, though not discussed.

collective-defense.rationale: Mutual defense pacts are not discussed in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation and occupation law is not discussed in the sources.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: State control of religious institutions is not discussed; religion is treated as a field for feminist reinterpretation.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The ceremonial role of heads of state is not discussed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Peace emphasis suggests reluctance to use force; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy arrangements like this are not discussed in the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred hereditary ruler contradicts equal rights and participation; and sources note colonial and customary male rulers curtailed women.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Class-aware analysis implies support for progressive taxation, so flat rates are disfavoured; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Sources attribute gender roles to social and colonial conditions rather than nature, which supports an environmental view of character; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Equal protection and accountability under the Protocol leave no room for rulers above the law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is outside the sources.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The classical mixed constitution is not discussed in the sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Participatory and egalitarian politics lean against leader cults; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Sources note that many feminists include men's roles, but custody law is not discussed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Class conflict inside socialist states is not discussed in the sources.

land-redistribution.rationale: Sources document that men controlled land and income under colonialism and that women farm most food, which supports giving land to those who work it.

refugee-return.rationale: Protocol protections for women in armed conflict and displacement imply support for return; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not addressed; ethnic claims over territory conflict with continental peace emphasis.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Rights-based feminisms, including Islamic feminists seeking equality in religion, would reject penalties for leaving religion; inferred from the Protocol's rights base.

women-must-cover.rationale: Feminists oppose compulsion over women's bodies, and even Islamic feminism works for equality, not mandatory covering by law.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity of kin peoples across borders is not discussed in the sources.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not discussed in the sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration versus local struggle is not discussed in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Stiwanism treats economic structure as one of several factors, not the main driver.

ban-cartels.rationale: Opposition to concentrated neo-colonial economic power suggests support; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Protocol protects women's rights against customary majorities, implying courts should constrain them.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The article records Kenya's #WeAre52 campaign for a two-thirds gender cap in governing bodies, and Article 9 of the Protocol requires women's participation in decision-making.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Women's historical role in international trade suggests openness over autarky; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Economic and social welfare rights for women favour binding labour standards; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Moral versus material incentives for work are not discussed in the sources.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Peace emphasis leans against armed vanguards; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Equal rights and participation conflict with inherited privilege, though titles are not discussed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nnaemeka's call for African women as knowledge producers on African terms supports teaching history from African centres.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Ogundipe-Leslie ascribed women's plight partly to imposed colonial structures and rejected defining African feminism through Euro-America.

patriotic-education.rationale: Teaching national loyalty in schools is not discussed in the sources.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Support for correcting historical injustice leaves little room for ending preferences; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not discussed in the sources.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalism's crisis capacity is not discussed in the sources.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Anti-imperial emphasis rejects cultivating influence over former colonies; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Not addressed; women's trading histories point against full delinking, anti-neocolonial thought toward it.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The theory that rich-country workers share in imperial profits is not discussed in the sources.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Protocol's non-discrimination principle and anti-discrimination aims reject private discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Protocol itself is a binding rights instrument that constrains government; Wikipedia reports 44 ratifications.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Opposition to colonial division and its effects suggests sympathy; not stated.

elective-rulers.rationale: Article 9 on participation in political processes and campaigns for women's seats assume elected leadership.

minority-veto.rationale: Nego-feminism favours compromise rather than veto power; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Rights-based accountability implies resistance to lawless rule; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliament versus monarch is not discussed; women's presence in parliaments is the concern.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not discussed in the sources, though Motherism values nature and nurture.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Use of animals for food or research is not discussed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The duty of the privileged to help the less fortunate is not discussed as such in the sources.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The tradition is built on women's participation in politics and decision-making, the opposite of withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Critical theory of mass culture is not part of the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony through culture is not discussed in the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Ogundipe-Leslie blamed colonial and neo-colonial structures for women's plight, consistent with extractive world economy; not stated as dependency theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Birth-based limits on office are not discussed in the sources.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party independence is not discussed in the sources.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Nnaemeka favours local priorities in development but no rejection of aid is stated.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Peace emphasis leans against irredentist demands; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Leadership by descendants of pre-colonial peoples over settlers is not discussed in the sources.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Constitutional anti-fascism is not discussed in the sources.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Comparing fascism and communism is not discussed in the sources.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: No stated position; opposition to racial hierarchy implies rejecting the denial of slavery's role.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument disputes are not discussed in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources say African feminists see men as facing hardships of their own and favour including them, though the programme centres women.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The Protocol treats violence against women as a distinct harm requiring protection, rejecting equivalence; inferred from its focus.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Nnaemeka rejects Western theory formation as imperial and holds African women do feminism on their own terms, which supports locally shaped institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Participatory and peace aims lean against a political army; inferred.

paid-care-work.rationale: Motherism and care emphases value nurture, and sources note women's unpaid labour burdens; payment for care is not stated directly.

filial-duty.rationale: Communalism and family values are central to African feminist writers such as Aidoo and Acholonu.

office-by-exam.rationale: Examination-based civil service is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Screening of foreign takeovers is not discussed in the sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Protocol covers equal rights in divorce, but fault versus no-fault grounds are not stated.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandates for delegates are not discussed in the sources.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed in the sources.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Customary land tenure disadvantaged women according to the sources, so adherents have no single view on communal land holding.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Budget approval rules are not discussed in the sources.

single-official-language.rationale: Linguistic diversity of African women's writing leans against single-language rules; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Foreign ownership of land is not discussed; the sources deal with women's access to land.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Stiwanism's focus on structural disadvantage suggests outcome-based concern; not stated.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Consumerism is not discussed in the sources.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Peace emphasis and concern for women in conflict make arming insurgents contrary to the position; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Anti-imperial stance opposes great powers intervening in other countries; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Opposition to neo-colonial economic power suggests agreement, though lobbying is not discussed.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: African feminists work with international donors while criticising Western agendas; no stated support for restrictions.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Motherism values motherhood but state natalism is not discussed.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on home purchases are not discussed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Economic and social welfare rights for women suggest sympathy; not stated.

democratic-peace.rationale: The democratic peace thesis is not discussed in the sources.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The duty to obey law is not discussed in the sources.

non-intervention.rationale: Nnaemeka rejects outside rescue interventions yet the Protocol is a regional rights norm, so adherents mix.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure by craft or industry is not discussed in the sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy claims against a minority conflict with non-discrimination and dignity.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Protocol regulates marriage in women's interest, so abolishing legal marriage is not its approach, and family is valued by many adherents.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Participation in decision-making presupposes access to information; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Localised production is not discussed, though women's food production and local trade are noted.

informal-organisation.rationale: Nnaemeka describes informal women's networks and savings groups, but the sources do not oppose permanent organisations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: African feminists rely on international and continental treaties like the Maputo Protocol, so primacy of national law is disfavoured.

religious-nation.rationale: Religious plurality in Africa and rights framing lean against it; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anti-imperial stance rejects tribute-style deference; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal sharing between regions is not discussed in the sources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The distinction between personal and productive property is not discussed in the sources.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold War anti-communism is not discussed in the sources.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The Protocol assigns duties to states but not on provider mix.

religion-illusion.rationale: The sources treat Islam and Christianity as fields that African feminists reinterpret from within rather than illusions to outgrow, which supports disagreement; secular strands such as Thiam's make a strong rejection unrepresentative.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Stiwanism's critique of neo-colonial structures leans against viewing capitalism as progressive; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Stiwanism links women's liberation to wider social transformation including class and neo-colonial structures.

socialized-care.rationale: Sources value motherhood and family while seeking recognition of women's burdens, so adherents are split.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed; multilingual writing tradition leans against purging.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with nations within a state are not discussed in the sources.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Nnaemeka describes cooperative savings groups but not a society reorganised in cooperative communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Policy settling majorities in minority regions conflicts with non-discrimination; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: A third economic way is not discussed in the sources as such.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical and religious land claims are not discussed in the sources.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No support in the sources; the commitment to dignity and anti-racism excludes denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Nyanzi notes most African feminists resist challenging heterosexism, but queer African feminists and rights framing oppose criminalisation, leaving adherents divided with a lean against.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The programme's insistence on participation and rights rules out suppressing opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Rights-based feminisms oppose punishing religious expression; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The article says colonialism weakened women's status and removed female chiefs' power, so adherents oppose colonial rule for the metropole's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; Islamic feminism does not address it in the sources.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Rights frameworks reject removal of rulers by force on religious grounds; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Article 9's right to participation and women's local organising support wide participation in decisions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Awa Thiam's multiple jeopardy holds that sex, class and colonial or racial oppression combine, and Wikipedia notes intersectionality is welcomed but judged insufficient.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Some queer African feminists back it, but the majority resist challenging heterosexism, so adherents are split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is not discussed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The left-right spectrum is not discussed in the sources.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Marxian theory of alienation is not discussed in the sources.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The article describes Islamic feminism in Africa working inside Islam for gender equality, so adherents reject claims of incompatibility with modern values.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Muslim, Christian and secular strands differ.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Nnaemeka criticises Western feminist fixation on veils, so adherents would be wary of dress bans, but state-school rules are not discussed.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Protection against violence and sexual harassment under the Protocol supports access to remedies; NDAs are not discussed.

social-market-economy.rationale: Protocol social and economic rights fit market economies with social protection; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Peace commitments suggest sympathy, but abolition is not stated.

rich-first.rationale: Stiwanism's concern with inclusive transformation leans against letting some grow rich first.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Equal participation conflicts with hereditary succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Nnaemeka describes women's rotating savings and mutual credit groups, which fits user-owned credit, but not the wider proposal.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Opposition to neo-colonial economic structures suggests support; austerity not directly discussed.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Motherism links motherhood, nature and nurture, and its aim of complementarity between humans and nature supports shared liberation.

reification.rationale: The theory of reification is not discussed in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Ownership of the press is not discussed in the sources.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Protocol relies on law and legal remedies for women; standing laws are inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: The sources hold no support for racial limits on voting; the tradition opposes colonial racial hierarchy.

online-participation.rationale: Internet deliberation is not discussed in the sources.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data on government decisions is not discussed in the sources.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The Protocol's marriage rules require free consent, which leans against restricting marriages; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a minority conflicts with non-discrimination and dignity.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition-based assemblies are not discussed in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The article describes Islamic revivalist feminists and others seeking gender equality within an Islamic framework, which is reinterpretation of religion.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Class analysis and opposition to neo-colonial economic power fit agreement; not stated.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Most African feminists resist challenging heterosexism, a minority back LGBT rights, so adherents are split.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Religion is a field of feminist engagement in Africa and not treated as something for the state to remove.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed; concern for violence against women suggests relying on protective institutions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational power sharing is not discussed in the sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Protocol assigns welfare duties to states, so charity alone is not favoured.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits for politicians are not discussed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not discussed in the sources.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is not discussed in the sources.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Nana Asma'u's women's education movement and Islamic feminists seeking equality indicate support for women's religious roles; leadership offices are not specified.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Maputo Protocol sets equal rights and shared responsibility between spouses in marriage as a core provision on marriage and divorce.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Voting rights for foreign residents are not discussed in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Rent caps are not discussed, though the Protocol covers the right to adequate housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Patents and copyright are not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Peace and participatory emphasis lean against drilled youth movements; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anti-imperial stance suggests agreement; not stated.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Protocol protection of women in conflict implies support for recognising mass atrocity; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Class analysis and women's unpaid labour fit rewarding work over ownership; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: No stated position; most adherents would not demand strict pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Sources show gender roles changing under colonialism, so continuity from ancient origins is not their view.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Only a few radical feminists address binary gender, so this is not a stated mainstream position.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The article says Africa's diversity rules out a single feminist theory, and stiwanism treats class, religion and marital status as shaping women's experiences.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring national martyrs is not discussed in the sources.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Politics as a cosmic struggle is not discussed in the sources.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Homelands and diasporas are not discussed in the sources used here.

culture-before-state.rationale: The order of cultural renewal and state-building is not discussed in the sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed apart from Islamic feminism, with no stated position on God language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Islamic feminists seek equality within religion, but adherents of other strands do not use scripture as the test, so they split.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Non-discrimination principle leans against reserving economic life to the majority; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Merging regions for one people is not discussed in the sources.

independent-unions.rationale: Women's autonomous organising is valued; independent unions specifically are inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The definition of socialism by workers' power is not discussed in the sources.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Rights to health and housing suggest public provision of essentials; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Bicameralism is not discussed in the sources.

municipal-property.rationale: Community ownership of the means of production is not discussed in the sources.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Confederal municipalism is not discussed in the sources.

family-wage.rationale: Valuing family and women's economic security suggests support, though the sources do not discuss wage levels.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation speed is not discussed in the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research is not discussed in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Untraceable payments are not discussed in the sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online pseudonymity is not discussed in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: The Protocol protects persons' dignity against states and customs; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Motherism and religion-inclusive feminisms point to a spiritual dimension; not stated for politics generally.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The legal basis of regional self-government is not discussed in the sources.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetically engineered crops are not discussed, though women's role in food production is stressed.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban density and the environment are not discussed in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Africana womanism emphasises Black women's own politics but others reject race organising, so adherents split.

racial-pride.rationale: Africana womanism, rooted in Black life, and the break from white feminism endorse pride in African ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Peace and anti-war emphasis suggests agreement; not stated.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Defining nations by language is not discussed in the sources.

communal-electorates.rationale: Equal citizen participation leans against separate communal electorates; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Fear of foreign partition plots is not discussed in the sources.

free-public-college.rationale: The Protocol's education provisions favour access; tuition is not discussed.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Polluter-pays taxation is not discussed in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: Motherism's emphasis on nurture and nature suggests agreement; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Motherism places motherhood and nurture at the core, and nego-feminism draws on maternal ideas, though not all strands claim distinct values.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secret versus open treaties are not discussed in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Capital flow controls are not discussed in the sources.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Protection from violence under the Protocol favours state monopoly over armed groups; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Refusal of orders in inter-state wars is not discussed in the sources.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Women's collective negotiating is valued, though labour bargaining is not discussed.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credit design is not discussed in the sources.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Social rights lean against binding limits on borrowing; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Ogundipe-Leslie's critique of neo-colonial structures supports reshaping international economic rules.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Programme uses state instruments like the Protocol rather than replacing the state; inferred.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Free experimentation among economic systems is not discussed in the sources.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural capital accounting is not discussed in the sources.

sacred-nation.rationale: The tradition is internally diverse and critical of national and customary power; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loan relief is not discussed in the sources.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Internal colonialism between regions is not discussed in the sources.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Nnaemeka resists Western universals, while the Protocol assumes shared rights, so adherents split.

public-service-media.rationale: Public broadcasting is not discussed in the sources.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The unity of religions is not discussed in the sources.

farm-price-support.rationale: Women's central role in food production suggests support for protecting farmers; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Peace emphasis leans against nuclear arsenals.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Protocol attention to violence against women, including in armed conflict, supports accountability for state abuses; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Limiting the vote by wealth contradicts equal participation rights and the sources' record of women excluded from land and income.

ban-fgm.rationale: The Maputo Protocol seeks an end to female genital mutilation and Wikipedia lists FGM among the major problems facing African women.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The Protocol includes rights to inheritance and widows' rights, and the sources document men's control of land under colonial and customary rule.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from the view that class combines with sex and race as oppressions; the sources do not say whether women should organise through a workers' party or broad movements.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; African feminisms engage with local languages and cultures but take no stand on regional language naming.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from African feminism's stress on collective and structural remedies against neo-colonial exploitation rather than individual suits; the sources never discuss pollution.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the claim that colonial and customary rule strengthened men's control, and from the Maputo Protocol's equality rights; adherents value African culture, so this is not strongly negative.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and no stated priority between environment and liberty; adherents are likely split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Criminal sentencing policy is outside what the sources address.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is about women's status on the African continent, not immigration policy.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The sources do not discuss union rules; concern for women in informal work is not tied to either position, so adherents are inferred as split.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents would weigh election integrity against exclusion of poor and rural women, so inferred as split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Adherents challenge patriarchal religious interpretation while valuing religious plurality, so equal state treatment of interpretations is inferred; the sources do not state it.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Feminists in this tradition stress substantive equality and structural change, so elections alone do not suffice; inferred.

premarital-sex.rationale: Wikipedia notes that sexuality is the issue on which strands differ most: some reject Western sexual liberation, others defend women's sexual autonomy.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The sources never discuss shutdowns; concern for women's rights and access suggests opposition, inferred from that.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Concern for women's poverty favours cash support, but the strand's structural critique makes replacing welfare programmes uncertain; inferred as split.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Maputo Protocol commits states to women's equal participation in political life, and equal political rights are a basic aim of the movement.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Wikipedia describes African feminists as divided: some criticise religion's role in patriarchy while others stress its place in African life and see religion as often supporting women.

race-social-construct.rationale: Awa Thiam's multiple jeopardy and the colonial account of oppression treat race as imposed by colonialism, though the sources do not discuss its scientific basis; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: The Maputo Protocol obliges states to adopt measures and institutions to advance women's rights, consistent with dedicated state bodies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The sources do not address first-come land claims; African feminists stress customary and communal land and women's rights to it, so inferred as against.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: The Maputo Protocol protects women in armed conflict and calls for justice for violations, so adherents would back international prosecution; the sources give no view on aggression trials.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The sources do not address scripture; the strand challenges patriarchal readings of religious and customary texts, so literal inerrancy is inferred as rejected.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The Maputo Protocol commits states to women's participation in political and decision-making processes, and African feminism seeks equality from the outset of post-colonial arrangements.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Not addressed; African feminism is often socialist-leaning and anti-neocolonial but critical of bureaucratic rule, so it is inferred as split.

indirect-election.rationale: The sources do not address electoral form; the strand pushes for direct women's political participation and quotas, so indirect selection is inferred as disfavoured.

national-church-status.rationale: The strand criticises institutions that entrench patriarchy and does not seek privileged status for churches; inferred, not stated in the sources.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; the strand is rooted in African cultures and anti-colonial, but strands differ on ethnic politics, so it is inferred as split.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The sources do not address disputed territories; adherents are split between self-determination and fixed post-colonial borders.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anti-colonial African movements broadly accepted inherited borders to avoid conflict, though the sources do not discuss this for African feminism; inferred.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed; the strand values communal life and critiques consumption but also seeks material improvement for women, so it is inferred as split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the strand defends indigenous cultures but also women's mobility, so it is inferred as split.

equal-conscription.rationale: The strand's commitment to equality of women and men implies equal obligations, though the sources never mention conscription; inferred.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: African feminism grounds its project in African cultures and histories, so a bond with ancestral land fits; inferred, since the sources do not discuss homeland as such.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The Maputo Protocol's rights to life, dignity and security of person are incompatible with killing suspects without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment with China is outside what African feminist sources address, and no position can be inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Protection of kin minorities abroad is not an African feminist theme; no position inferred.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Resource ownership is not addressed beyond critiques of colonial land control, so adherents have no stated view.

self-ownership.rationale: Bodily autonomy and control over one's own labour are implied by the Protocol's rights and Ogundipe-Leslie's critique of women's burdens, but the sources do not use the self-ownership framing.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Consumption taxes are not discussed in the sources; no position inferred.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Targeted versus universal social spending is not addressed; adherents could favour either.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The sources do not address party or leader politics, and strands differ on the state.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Business privilege is not discussed in the sources; no position inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Religious-denominational politics is not addressed; strands differ on the role of religion.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: African feminism seeks change rooted in African culture without rejecting modernity, so a combination is inferred; the sources do not state it for technology.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: The Maputo Protocol's equal rights within marriage, including separation and divorce, imply women may end a marriage without needing the husband's consent.

national-resource-control.rationale: Feminists in this tradition treat neo-colonial structures as a source of women's oppression, from which a preference for national control is inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Ogundipe-Leslie's focus on structural inequality suggests distribution should be judged by outcomes as well as process; inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: International financial taxes are not addressed in the sources; no position inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Multiple-jeopardy analysis treats racism as still combining with sex and class, so adherents would reject the claim; inferred rather than stated about racial groups.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Natural-law doctrine on unjust laws is not addressed; adherents challenge customary and statutory law but not in these terms.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Automation and reduced paid work are not discussed in the sources.

multipolar-world.rationale: Opposition to neo-colonial structures suggests support for a less dominated world order; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The sources do not address value theory; no position inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Patriotism is not a theme in the sources; the class analysis of Ogundipe-Leslie does not settle it.

material-over-identity.rationale: African feminists hold that sex, class and race oppressions combine, so they reject concentrating on material interests alone.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Party-led market socialism is not addressed in the sources; no position inferred.

missingStatements.text: Female genital mutilation should be prohibited by law.
missingStatements.rationale: The Maputo Protocol seeks an end to female genital mutilation and Wikipedia lists FGM among the major problems facing African women.

missingStatements.text: Women should have the same legal right as men to inherit and own land.
missingStatements.rationale: The Protocol includes rights to inheritance and widows' rights, and the sources document men's control of land under colonial and customary rule.

missingStatements.text: Women's rights are best advanced by negotiating with men and community institutions rather than by confronting them.
missingStatements.rationale: Nnaemeka's nego-feminism and snail-sense feminism stress negotiation and working with men, though stiwanism also demands wider transformation.
missingStatements.declined: A question of method rather than position, and contested within African feminism itself.

notes: Strands diverge: nego-feminism and Motherism stress negotiation, complementarity and family; stiwanism and Thiam stress structural and class transformation; a minority of queer African feminists challenge heterosexism that most others leave unquestioned. Sources opened were partly secondary (Wikipedia); only Nnaemeka's essay is a primary text, and the Maputo Protocol's article wording was not read directly.
